chapter_theme: Songs at Thiruppandikkodumudi (திருப்பாண்டிக்கொடுமுடி): a short plea to escape the sea of births made by the two deeds, and a love scene in which the poet is drawn to women like a needle to a magnet.

932.reading: A short song: the poet asks whether, instead of drowning in the sea of births made by the two kinds of deeds and tossing in suffering, he will by the radiance of grace's compassion firmly reach the goal. The praise calls Murugan hard for Hari and Brahma to know, easy for his devotees, the wondrous lover, the teacher who gave grace to Siva as guru, the Kumara of Kodumudi.
932.nuance: அரியயற்கு அறிதற்கு அரியானே, அடியவர்க்கு எளிய: hard for the gods, easy for devotees, a pairing of the hymns. குருவெனச் சிவனுக்கு அருள் போதா keeps the teaching of Siva in a single phrase.

933.reading: The poet describes falling to women with glory-lily hands and bangles as a needle falls to a magnet, their sandal-scented hair like dark cloud, spear eyes reaching their earrings, and the touching of garments and holding of breasts, and asks whether he will not give up those embraces. The praise names Murugan of Vayalur, who grants men and the king of gods what each desires, the lover who bowed to the small feet of the deer-like girl in the bamboo-fringed millet field, and the lord praised in bards' words to whom the lord of Pandikkodumudi with serpent-bound hair is drawn as to a supreme guru.
933.nuance: ஊசி காந்தத்து உறவென வீழ்ந்து: the needle drawn to the magnet makes desire a force the poet does not choose. மான் சிற்றடி தொழு மதிகாமி: Murugan bowing to Valli's small feet reverses the usual direction of worship. The last lines on Siva of Kodumudi are hard to divide.
